newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-CRICKET- Allott has one-day debut to remember.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-CRICKET- Allott has one-day debut to remember.

text.p: NAPIER, Feb 26 - No matter how long Geoff Allott plays one-day cricket for New Zealand, he'll never forget his first match against England in Napier last night.
Lively left armer Allott was required to bowl the last over of the match, with England needing eight runs to win not only the game but also the five-match series.
Allott kept his nerve, New Zealand took two wickets and with two needed off the final ball, he beat Darren Gough's stroke, the batsmen scampered a bye and the match was tied.
It was New Zealand's third tied one-dayer in 275 matches -- the others were against Pakistan in Auckland in 1994 and against Sri Lanka in Sharjah late last year.
Chasing New Zealand's 237, England finished on 237 for eight, with Allott bouncing back from a nightmare start to take two for 50 off nine overs.
"I knew I had to come back for the team's sake," Allott said last night.
"It was a question of me getting my act together and bowling a better length."
Allott's first three overs cost 30 as England openers Nick Knight and captain Mike Atherton climbed into a succession of half volleys and half trackers from Allott and Simon Doull.

When he clutched a sharp return catch from Knight for his first one-day wicket it helped put the brakes on a flying England start, as he bowled his final four overs of his first spell at a cost of just seven runs.
After allrounder Chris Harris had taken three for 20 off 10 overs in a marvellous spell in mid-innings, it was left to Allott and fellow one-day fledgling Heath Davis to complete the job.
Davis impressed in the first one-dayer at Christchurch and he built on that with a lively, accurate effort last night.
England needed 62 off the last 10 overs and lefthander Graham Thorpe pushed England towards victory with 55 off 61 balls.
Then Allott and Davis had to contend with Craig White and Dominic Cork, who added a crucial 58 in 61 balls for the seventh wicket to carry England within touching distance of the win.
Davis' last two overs cost just 10 while Allott, despite a fourth-ball hiccup when Robert Croft slammed him to the mid wicket boundary, completed the job.
Allott, who only knew he was playing half an hour before the start, knows he'll benefit from what happened last night.
"It's something I really enjoyed," he said.
"Experience wise it's going to be invaluable for me. Although you play Shell Cup one-dayers and you can have great excitement at the aed, this is something I'm going to learn a hell of a lot from."
The result left the New Zealanders with mixed emotions -- delight at being more competitive than in the two earlier defeats in the series but disappointment at losing the chance to win the rubber.
"It was pretty exciting, but we came to win and it didn't quite go the way we'd planned. Obviously a win would have been more satisfying," Allott said.
Captain Lee Germon, conceding New Zealand's total was "20-30" runs short of his target, was pleased the series can still be saved.
"Overall I'm very happy the series is still alive, we've still got a chance to square it," he said.
"238 was a very gettable target on that deck. I was very happy with the bowling and fielding and we can bat even better than we did.
"Although the guys are disappointed they can hold their heads high and be positive about the remainder of the series."
The result can't hide some disturbing aspects about the New Zealand performance.
The batsmen threw away a splendid start, when Nathan Astle and Bryan Young put on 50 in 53 balls for the first wicket.

Germon, who went up to No 3 in the order, was stumped off a wide, Stephen Fleming and Chris Cairns gifted their wickets away and it could have proved costly, but for Allott's and Davis' late night effort with the ball.
Doull's bowling in the last two one-dayers has been poor while Astle's value as a backup medium pacer has been non-existent; he has bowled 7.3 overs in the three games and taken none for 62.
England aren't particularly upset at having a series-clinching chance elude them.
"I'm pleased we gave ourselves a great opportunity to win," Atherton said.
"We're slightly disappointed we didn't get there, but very pleased at the way we battled through."
New Zealand must win the fourth match at Eden Park in Auckland on Saturday to maintain their hopes of squaring the series.
